hypothesis: The parent assigns a thread to each target and performs its full source-particle accumulation serially. Giving each target to a warp distributes that traversal across 32 lanes and exposes more target warps across CTAs; a warp-local reduction may reduce per-target serial work, though its reduction overhead and altered summation order must be measured.
notes: The supplied baseline observation is valid on all 11 correctness cases and reports a three-repeat mean of 0.0018526411283622502 seconds. This candidate has not been measured. The launch uses 256 threads per CTA and 8 target warps per CTA, with no shared-memory tiling; each warp reaches the reduction even for an out-of-range target, and only lane 0 writes the complete particle state for an in-range target. Official correctness checks should precede timing comparisons.
transformations: Map each warp to one target using the global warp index; configure 256 threads and 8 target warps per CTA.
Have each lane accumulate source indices lane + 32k, skipping the self pair and bounding traversal by n.
Reduce the three force components with full-warp shuffle-down operations; lane 0 integrates and writes the full Particle record for valid targets.
